label: Trino

catalogEnrichments._description: When KDPS provisions the catalog it names it after the release and namespace, so the rendered Trino catalog must point at that name rather than the one the platform context advertises. Applied here, server-side, because it is the same value the provisioning step derives.
catalogEnrichments.name: iceberg-provisioned-warehouse

variables.comment: OpenShift: worker autoscaling reads metrics from the platform's built-in (user-workload) monitoring via the thanos-querier CLUSTER endpoint (:9091). The KEDA SA is bound to cluster-monitoring-view, so :9091 is the correct port (the :9092 tenancy port returns HTTP 400 for a cluster-view token and needs a per-request namespace param KEDA does not send). Verified on CRC: :9091 + bearer token returns the trino_* metrics. On vanilla K8s the kube-prometheus-stack address above is used instead.
variables.name: keda.thanos.serverAddress

variables.comment: Secret holding a bearer token for a ServiceAccount bound to the cluster-monitoring-view ClusterRole; consumed by the KEDA TriggerAuthentication on OpenShift. Operator-provided (see Cluster prerequisites), defaulting to this convention name.
variables.name: keda.thanos.tokenSecret

variables.comment: true only when Trino does NOT terminate TLS itself. Gates the forwarded-header trust below: with TLS on the coordinator, trusting X-Forwarded-Proto would let anything inside the cluster reach the plain HTTP port and claim the request arrived over TLS — the very check that guards authenticated traffic.
variables.name: tlsHttpsDisabled

bindings.name: ingress-setup
bindings._description: Writes the canonical ingress shape every KDPS chart accepts. The `hosts[]` entry uses the rich object form `{host, paths[]}` so OpenMetadata- and Trino-style charts work out of the box; the Superset chart's template was made shape-tolerant (accepts string OR object) in chart >= 0.12.25.

bindings.name: ingress-nginx-tuning
bindings._description: Backslash-escaped dots in the leaf key — the UI binding engine (bindings.ts:pathToParts) treats backslash-dot as a literal dot so the rendered values look like `ingress.annotations: { "nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffer-size": "..." }`.

bindings.name: keda-enable
bindings.comment: server.keda.enabled, minReplicaCount and maxReplicaCount are wizard fields (Autoscaling group).

bindings.name: service-monitor-enable
bindings.comment: serviceMonitor.enabled is the 'Collect metrics' wizard field.

Default (vanilla Kubernetes) KEDA triggers — scrape the kube-prometheus-stack Prometheus directly, no auth. Gated on isVanillaK8s so they are used everywhere EXCEPT a confirmed OpenShift cluster (where the openshift variant below takes over).
bindings.name: keda-triggers

bindings.comment: OpenShift KEDA triggers — same queries, but pointed at the thanos-querier tenancy endpoint (platform user-workload monitoring) with authModes=bearer and an authenticationRef to the TriggerAuthentication below. Gated on isOpenShift (fail-CLOSED: only a confirmed OpenShift cluster).
bindings.name: keda-triggers-openshift

bindings.comment: OpenShift only: turn on the chart's KEDA TriggerAuthentication (bearer token from the SA-token Secret) so the thanos-authenticated triggers above can read platform monitoring.
bindings.name: keda-trigger-auth-openshift

targets.comment: Only when the operator typed a keystore password. Left blank, KDPS generates one and the chart's init container appends it from the Secret — writing an empty key= line here would shadow nothing but is noise at best.

Flags only. The truststore SECRET is deliberately NOT set from this release's keystore: it is the CA bundle KDPS wires from the platform context (trino-truststore), and repointing it at the server keystore would leave Trino unable to verify the Keycloak JWKS endpoint or Ranger — breaking the very OIDC path TLS is being enabled for.

bindings.comment: Edge-terminated TLS only: Trino then has to believe the router about the original scheme. Skipped once Trino terminates TLS itself — see tlsHttpsDisabled.
bindings.name: trust-proxy-headers
iceberg-catalog
bindings._description: Trino 'iceberg' catalog on the Platform Context's Apache Polaris REST catalog. The region is written even without an S3 endpoint override: Trino's native S3 filesystem resolves a region when the catalog is constructed, before any table is loaded, so vended credentials do not remove the need for it and the connector fails to start without one. The OAuth2 client credential is NOT written here: the view fills polarisCredential.* and the clemlab-trino chart (>=1.43.9) appends iceberg.rest-catalog.oauth2.credential=${ENV:POLARIS_CLIENT_ID}:${ENV:POLARIS_CLIENT_SECRET} from a Secret — the view interpolator would blank a literal ${ENV:...}.

bindings.name: iceberg-s3-credential-inline
bindings._description: Static S3 keys for a Polaris catalog on a no-STS object store (Ozone S3 gateway / MinIO). The chart (>=1.43.10) exposes them as ICEBERG_S3_ACCESS_KEY/ICEBERG_S3_SECRET_KEY from a Secret, appends s3.aws-access-key/s3.aws-secret-key=${ENV:...} to the iceberg catalog and turns Polaris credential vending off there.

KDPS-provisioned access. The provisioning step runs before the chart is installed: it mints this release's Polaris identity, creates the catalog and bucket named <release>-<namespace> unless creation was turned off, and writes <release>-polaris-credential with client_id/client_secret.
bindings.name: iceberg-provisioned-credentials

bindings._description: The same Secret also carries access_key/secret_key, but the provisioning step writes those two ONLY when the operator supplied a static S3 access key. Pointing the chart at them regardless makes it mount env vars from keys that do not exist, and every pod fails with CreateContainerConfigError before it starts. Gated on the same form field the provisioning step reads.
bindings.name: iceberg-provisioned-s3-credential
hadoop-group-mapping-toggle
bindings._description: Sets hadoopConf.groupMapping.enabled — gates the init-container that splices LdapGroupsMapping into core-site.xml (chart >= 1.43.0).

bindings.name: hadoop-group-mapping-ldap-props
bindings._description: Map every Hadoop LdapGroupsMapping form field to its helm path. All paths under hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.* are read by the trino chart's init-hadoop-conf-overlay init container.

form.name: openshiftOptions
form.label: OpenShift
form.help: OpenShift-specific options. Only shown when KDPS detects the cluster is OpenShift.

fields.name: runAsUser
fields.label: Run pods as a specific UID (optional)
fields.help: Leave blank (recommended): OpenShift's restricted-v2 SCC assigns an arbitrary non-root UID from the project's range automatically. Set a UID only if you must pin one — it MUST fall inside the namespace's openshift.io/sa.scc.uid-range annotation, otherwise admission rejects the pods.

form.name: nameOverride
form.label: Name override
form.help: Appended to the release name to form the full name (e.g. <release>-clemlab-trino).

fields.name: serviceMonitor.enabled
fields.label: Collect metrics (ServiceMonitor)
fields.help: Lets OpenShift monitoring scrape Trino; needs the monitoring-edit role in the project. Required by worker autoscaling: turn autoscaling off to turn this off.

fields.name: monitoring.discovery
fields.label: Discover monitoring stack
fields.help: Finds the Prometheus already running on the cluster (any namespace, any release name) and fills the fields below from it.

fields.name: monitoring.namespace
fields.label: Monitoring namespace
fields.help: Namespace of the Prometheus stack, or where KDPS installs one when none is found.

fields.name: monitoring.release
fields.label: Monitoring release (Helm)
fields.help: Release of the Prometheus stack: builds the Prometheus address when none is given below, and is put on the ServiceMonitors as their release label.

fields.name: monitoring.url
fields.label: Prometheus address
fields.help: Address the autoscaler queries, filled by discovery. Leave blank to use http://<release>-prometheus.<namespace>.svc:9090.

fields.name: serviceMonitor.enabled
fields.label: Collect metrics (ServiceMonitor)
fields.help: Lets Prometheus scrape Trino. Required by worker autoscaling.

fields.name: monitoring.serviceMonitorLabels
fields.label: ServiceMonitor labels
fields.help: Labels the Prometheus selects ServiceMonitors by, as key=value pairs separated by commas. Filled by discovery.

fields.name: keda.discovery
fields.label: Discover KEDA
fields.help: Finds the KEDA operator already on the cluster, which worker autoscaling then uses. When none is found, KDPS installs KEDA in the namespace below.

fields.name: keda.namespace
fields.label: KEDA namespace
fields.help: Namespace KDPS installs KEDA into, as no KEDA operator was found.

fields.name: internalSharedSecret
fields.label: Internal shared secret
fields.help: Value of internal-communication.shared-secret, which secures communication between Trino nodes.

fields.name: webUi.enabled
fields.label: Enable the web UI
fields.help: Sets web-ui.enabled in Trino (the UI is available by default).

fields.name: ingress.enabled
fields.label: Enable Ingress
fields.help: Expose the service through a Kubernetes Ingress. Required when an authentication profile (OIDC / LDAP-over-SSL) is selected in Step 1 — OAuth callbacks need a public hostname and HTTPS.

fields.name: ingress.ingressClassName
fields.label: Ingress class
fields.help: Ingress class name (e.g. 'nginx', 'openshift-default'). Leave empty for the default controller.

fields.name: ingress.host
fields.label: Hostname (DNS)
fields.help: Public DNS name the edge routes to (e.g. service.example.com). On OpenShift this becomes the Route host and must sit under the cluster ingress domain (…apps-<cluster>) to resolve — or leave it blank to let OpenShift auto-assign a reachable host. Under OIDC/OAuth this host is also the login redirect (https://<host>/oauth2/callback), so register it in the identity provider.

fields.name: ingress.path
fields.label: HTTP path
fields.help: Base path for the Ingress (usually '/').

fields.name: ingress.tlsMode
fields.label: TLS mode
fields.help: Pick how this service gets its TLS leaf. Recommended path is **Sign via cert-manager** when cert-manager is installed in the cluster (auto-renewal, standard K8s pattern). Fall back to **Sign with Company CA** (if you've uploaded one to the PKI registry) or **Sign with Ambari Internal CA** (testing only, browsers will warn). Options whose backing system isn't installed are hidden automatically. TLS is mandatory when an auth profile is selected in Step 1.

options.label: Source from external Secret store (Vault, ESO)
None (HTTP only — not allowed with auth)

fields.name: ingress.tlsSecret
fields.label: Existing TLS Secret name
fields.help: Name of a kubernetes.io/tls Secret already present in the release namespace. The chart references it via ingress.tls[].secretName.

fields.name: ingress.tlsUpload.cert
fields.label: TLS certificate (PEM, leaf + chain)
fields.help: Paste the full chain (leaf first). Saved as tls.crt in the new Secret.

fields.name: ingress.tlsUpload.key
fields.label: TLS private key (PEM)
fields.help: Paste the private key matching the certificate above. Saved as tls.key.

fields.name: ingress.tlsUpload.secretName
fields.label: Target Secret name
fields.help: Name of the kubernetes.io/tls Secret the view will create from the uploaded cert/key. Leave blank to use the default `<releaseName>-ingress-tls` (computed server-side at deploy time).

fields.name: ingress.tlsSelfSign.caName
fields.label: Company CA
fields.help: Pick a Company Issuing CA from the PKI registry. The view mints a leaf TLS cert signed by this CA before installing the chart. CAs are stored as Kubernetes Secrets in the `ambari-pki` namespace labeled `ambari.clemlab.com/resource-type=issuing-ca`. Upload CAs via Cluster security → Certificate Authorities.

fields.name: ingress.tlsSelfSign.validityDays
fields.label: Leaf validity (days)
fields.help: How long the minted leaf certificate is valid. Capped server-side at 825 (CA/Browser Forum baseline).

fields.name: ingress.certManager.issuerName
fields.label: ClusterIssuer
fields.help: Pick a cert-manager ClusterIssuer or Issuer. The view writes a Certificate resource pre-install; cert-manager mints the Secret and auto-renews it before expiry.

fields.name: ingress.certManager.validityDays
fields.label: Leaf validity (days)
fields.help: Validity in days. Translated to durationHours on the Certificate resource. cert-manager renews at duration/6 before expiry.

fields.name: ingress.externalSecret.secretStoreName
fields.label: SecretStore
fields.help: Pick an external-secrets SecretStore or ClusterSecretStore. Typically Vault-backed for TLS leaves (PKI mount).

fields.name: ingress.externalSecret.remoteKey
fields.label: Remote key / path
fields.help: Path/key in the upstream store. For Vault PKI: 'pki/issue/<role>'. For Vault KV: 'secret/data/tls/<name>'. For AWS Secrets Manager: the secret name.

fields.name: ingress.externalSecret.refreshInterval
fields.label: Refresh interval
fields.help: ESO refresh cadence. e.g. '1h', '15m', '0' (no periodic refresh).

fields.name: ingressTuning
fields.label: Ingress tuning (nginx)

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBufferSize
fields.label: proxy-buffer-size
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffer-size. Leave blank to use chart default (16k under OIDC/OAuth, otherwise nginx default 4k/8k). Bump if you see 502 + 'upstream sent too big header' on OAuth callbacks.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBuffersNumber
fields.label: proxy-buffers-number
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffers-number. Total response buffers = number × size.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBusyBuffersSize
fields.label: proxy-busy-buffers-size
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-busy-buffers-size. Should be ≥ proxy-buffer-size and ≤ total buffer capacity.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBodySize
fields.label: proxy-body-size
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size. Maximum request body the proxy accepts (e.g. '64m'). Bump for large uploads / file imports.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyReadTimeout
fields.label: proxy-read-timeout (seconds)
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout. Bump for long-running queries (Trino, Superset). Default 60.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyConnectTimeout
fields.label: proxy-connect-timeout (seconds)
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-connect-timeout. Time the proxy waits when opening a connection to the backend pod.

Advanced — usually leave blank. nginx ingress annotations (proxy buffers / timeouts). Chart-side defaults are sensible for the common case; expand if you need to override (large headers on OAuth, long-running queries, big uploads).

fields.name: tls.https.enabled
fields.label: Enable internal HTTPS
fields.help: On by default: Trino terminates TLS itself (keystore signed by the internal CA). The OpenShift Route then uses passthrough, and internal clients (Superset, dbt, OpenMetadata) must use https on the HTTPS port. Turned off, TLS stops at the edge: authenticated traffic, tokens included, crosses the pod network in clear text.

fields.name: tls.https.autoGenerate
fields.label: Generate the keystore
fields.help: When on, Ambari issues a certificate signed by its internal CA and stores it in a Kubernetes Secret.

fields.name: tls.https.secretName
fields.label: Keystore Secret (optional)
fields.help: Name of the Secret that holds the keystore. Blank: <release>-https.

fields.name: tls.https.password
fields.label: Keystore password
fields.help: Leave blank to generate a random one.

fields.name: tls.https.keystorePath
fields.label: Path used by Trino
fields.help: Value set as server.config.https.keystore.path.

fields.name: tls.https.keystoreType
fields.label: Keystore format (JKS/PKCS12/PEM)
fields.help: Storage format of the server certificate. PEM creates tls.crt/tls.key/ca.crt.

fields.name: server.workers
fields.label: Number of workers
fields.help: Fixed number of workers (at least 1), used when worker autoscaling is off.

fields.name: server.keda.enabled
fields.label: Worker autoscaling
fields.help: Adds and removes workers with the load (KEDA). Off: a fixed number of workers (Worker resources).

fields.name: server.keda.maxReplicaCount
fields.label: Maximum workers
fields.help: Must be at least the minimum.

fields.name: accessControl.type
fields.label: Enable Access Control
fields.help: Access control for the Trino coordinator. 'Disabled (allow all)' runs Trino with its built-in allow-all system access control (no restrictions); 'Ranger' enforces the policies of the selected Platform Context's Ranger. NOTE: the value 'properties' is the chart's generic file/properties mode — combined with the allow-all line below it means 'no access control'.

fields.name: accessControl.properties
fields.label: Access control properties
fields.help: Contents of the coordinator's access-control.properties. Defaults to Trino's built-in allow-all (no restrictions), which is what 'Disabled (allow all)' means. Advanced operators may override it (e.g. a file-based rules provider). Required by the chart whenever access control type is 'properties'.

fields.name: rangerAdminUrl
fields.label: Ranger admin
fields.help: The Ranger of the selected Platform Context (right panel) whose policies Trino's plugin enforces. Resolved by KDPS from the context.

fields.name: tagSync.enabled
fields.label: Sync Atlas tags to Trino
fields.help: Projects the Platform Context's Atlas classifications onto Trino's Ranger service so tag-based masking, row-filtering and access policies apply to Trino the way they do for Hive/Impala. On by default when the context exposes Atlas tags. KDPS resolves the Ranger endpoint and credentials from the context; you only turn this on or off.

fields.name: hiveCatalog.enabled
fields.label: Enable Hive catalog
fields.help: When ON, KDPS creates a Trino 'hive' catalog connected to the Hive Metastore of the selected Platform Context (right panel). Auto-enabled when the selected context exposes Hive.

fields.name: hiveCatalog.metastoreUri
fields.label: Hive Metastore URI
fields.help: Delivered by KDPS from the selected Platform Context. Toggle Override only to point the catalog at a specific metastore (for example an external context without an Ambari to resolve it).

fields.name: hive.externalKeytabSecret
fields.label: External Trino service keytab Secret
fields.help: Only for an EXTERNAL platform context (no Ambari to issue keytabs), e.g. a CDP backend in a DIFFERENT Kerberos realm. Pick a Kubernetes Secret in the release namespace holding key 'service.keytab' (the Trino SERVICE keytab issued by the backend realm's KDC). This is the Trino service identity — it mounts globally at /etc/security/keytabs/service.keytab and is used for EVERY Kerberos-authenticated backend Trino talks to: Hive metastore, HDFS, the Ranger plugin, and any other federated ODP service (not Hive only). Providing it selects PRE_PROVISIONED mode with your keytab instead of an Ambari-issued one; leave blank for a same-realm MANAGED (Ambari) context. Set the matching principal in the field below. Create it first, e.g.: kubectl -n <ns> create secret generic trino-cdp-keytab --from-file=service.keytab=./trino.keytab.

fields.name: hive.externalKeytabPrincipal
fields.label: External Trino service principal
fields.help: The Kerberos principal inside the external keytab above — the identity Trino authenticates AS to Hive / HDFS / Ranger. Set it per deploy so each Trino service can carry its own principal (not a shared/generic one). If left blank, KDPS falls back to a 'principal' key in the Secret. Only used when an external keytab is selected.

fields.name: hadoopGroupMapping
fields.label: Hadoop LDAP group mapping
fields.help: Resolves Hadoop groups from an LDAP/FreeIPA directory. Needed for group-based Ranger policies to apply to Trino queries (the Trino container has no SSSD). See HADOOP-LDAP-GROUP-MAPPING.md.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.enabled
fields.label: Enable LDAP group mapping
fields.help: When on, an init container merges the LdapGroupsMapping properties into core-site.xml when the pod starts. Needs Trino chart 1.43.0 or later.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.url
fields.label: LDAP URL
fields.help: LDAP/IPA endpoint, e.g. ldap://ipa.example.com:389. For LDAPS use ldaps://...:636 and make sure the CA is in Trino's truststore.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.bindUser
fields.label: Bind user
fields.help: DN of the service account that queries the directory (IPA hides memberOf from anonymous reads, so an authenticated bind is required), e.g. uid=hadoop-group-mapping,cn=users,cn=accounts,dc=example,dc=com

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.bindPasswordSecret.name
fields.label: Secret holding the password
fields.help: Kubernetes Secret in the target namespace (create it beforehand) holding the bind account's password. The chart mounts it read-only at /etc/hadoop/ldap-bind/password.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.bindPasswordSecret.key
fields.label: Key in the Secret
fields.help: Key of the Secret that holds the password (default 'password').

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.baseDn
fields.label: Search base DN
fields.help: Search base for users and groups, e.g. (FreeIPA) cn=accounts,dc=example,dc=com

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.userSearchFilter
fields.label: User filter (advanced)
fields.help: {0} is replaced by the user name. Change it only for a non-IPA directory.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.groupSearchFilter
fields.label: Group filter (advanced)
fields.help: LDAP filter that lists the groups. The default works with FreeIPA/RHIDM.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.memberAttr
fields.label: Member attribute (advanced)
fields.help: LDAP attribute holding the DNs of a group's members. FreeIPA: 'member'.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.cacheSeconds
fields.label: Group cache (seconds, advanced)
fields.help: How long the Hadoop client caches resolved groups.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.negativeCacheSeconds
fields.label: Negative cache (seconds, advanced)
fields.help: How long users without groups are cached (spares the directory).

fields.name: icebergCatalog.enabled
fields.label: Enable Iceberg catalog (Polaris REST)
fields.help: When ON, KDPS creates a Trino 'iceberg' catalog backed by the Apache Polaris REST catalog of the selected Platform Context (right panel), so Trino reads and writes Iceberg tables natively. Auto-enabled when the selected context exposes Polaris (ODP: the Ambari-managed POLARIS service). Prerequisites on the Polaris side: polaris.realm-context.require-header=false (Trino cannot send the realm header) and the Polaris TLS CA in the Trino truststore.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.provision
fields.label: Let KDPS create the catalog and its bucket
fields.help: ON (default): KDPS gives this release its own Polaris identity and creates a catalog and object-store bucket named after the release and namespace. Re-installing the same release re-uses them instead of creating more. OFF: nothing is created — KDPS only mints the identity and grants it on the catalog named below, which is how you attach a release to a catalog you already manage.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.restUri
fields.label: Polaris REST catalog URI
fields.help: Delivered by KDPS from the selected Platform Context (for example https://polaris-host:8443/api/catalog). Toggle Override only for a context without an Ambari to resolve it.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.warehouse
fields.label: Polaris catalog (warehouse)
fields.help: Name of the Polaris catalog Trino mounts as its 'iceberg' catalog. When KDPS creates the catalog it is named after the release and namespace and this field is ignored; with creation off, override it with the name of the catalog you want this release to use.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.credentialSecret
fields.label: Existing Polaris credential Secret
fields.help: Optional. A Kubernetes Secret in the release namespace holding keys 'client_id' and 'client_secret' of a Polaris principal granted a catalog role on the catalog above. When set, it takes precedence over the Client ID / Client secret fields below. Create it first, e.g.: kubectl -n <ns> create secret generic trino-polaris --from-literal=client_id=... --from-literal=client_secret=...

fields.name: icebergCatalog.clientId
fields.label: Polaris client ID
fields.help: OAuth2 client id of the Polaris principal Trino authenticates as (Polaris internal authentication). KDPS stores it in a chart-managed Kubernetes Secret and the catalog references it as ${ENV:POLARIS_CLIENT_ID} — the secret never appears in the catalog ConfigMap.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.clientSecret
fields.label: Polaris client secret
fields.help: OAuth2 client secret of the principal above.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.s3Endpoint
fields.label: Object store (S3 endpoint)
fields.help: Where the catalog's Iceberg tables are stored. Delivered by KDPS from the selected Platform Context's Ozone S3 gateway, the same store Polaris on the cluster uses. Toggle Override to point at another S3-compatible store; leave the override BLANK to use AWS S3 — then supply AWS credentials in the override group below.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.s3Region
fields.label: S3 region
fields.help: Region string sent with S3 requests. Any value works for Ozone; use the real region for AWS S3.

fields.name: icebergObjectStoreOverride
fields.label: Object store override (AWS / other S3)
fields.help: Only for a store that is not the context's Ozone: AWS S3 or another S3-compatible service. Credentials given here are used to create the bucket and are handed to Trino when the store cannot vend them through Polaris (no STS).

fields.name: icebergCatalog.s3CredentialSecret
fields.label: Existing S3 credential Secret
fields.help: Kubernetes Secret in the release namespace with keys 'access_key' and 'secret_key'. When set, it takes precedence over the two fields below and KDPS disables Polaris credential vending for this catalog.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.s3AccessKey
fields.label: S3 access key
fields.help: Static S3 access key. Stored in a chart-managed Kubernetes Secret and referenced as ${ENV:ICEBERG_S3_ACCESS_KEY}.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.s3SecretKey
fields.label: S3 secret key
fields.help: Secret key matching the access key above.

fields.name: dynamicCatalogs.enabled
fields.label: Allow catalogs to be created at runtime (CREATE CATALOG, no restart)
fields.help: Turns on Trino dynamic catalog management: the coordinator keeps a writable catalog store seeded from the catalogs below, so CREATE CATALOG / DROP CATALOG work immediately without a restart, and Ranger authorises them per user (catalog-level create/drop). Catalogs created only at runtime do not survive a pod restart - define them in this section to keep them. Needs chart 1.43.12 or later; the deploy is refused otherwise.

fields.name: kdps.serviceUser.enabled
fields.label: Let KDPS manage catalogs on the running Trino as the logged-in operator
fields.help: Adds a dedicated Trino login for KDPS (a file password user beside your LDAP/OIDC/Kerberos setup) and grants it 'impersonate' in Ranger. The Catalogs action on the release then runs CREATE/DROP CATALOG as you, so Ranger decides what you may do. Needs chart 1.43.13 or later and Trino HTTPS (on by default).

fields.name: customCatalogs.refs
fields.label: Reusable catalogs
fields.help: Catalogs defined once on the Trino Catalogs page and attached here. Each selected catalog's properties are copied into this release at deploy time (the release keeps that copy until you re-apply it from Upgrade/Config). Add a catalog to the list from the Trino Catalogs page.

fields.name: customCatalogs.text
fields.label: Additional Trino catalogs
fields.help: One section per catalog: a [name] header followed by that catalog's .properties lines. Each becomes a Trino catalog of that name and any connector Trino supports will work. connector.name is required. The Hive and Iceberg catalogs above are built by KDPS from the platform context - configure them there, not here. Do not paste credentials inline: put them in a Secret and reference ${ENV:VAR}.

description: Distributed SQL query engine for big data. Run ANSI SQL queries across Hive, S3, RDBMS and other sources at scale.

featureChartVersions._comment: Atlas tag sync renders a tag-projector CronJob that only exists from 1.43.11; on an older chart the toggle would deploy cleanly and do nothing.

platformOps._description: When Atlas tag sync is on, KDPS mints a Secret {user,password} in the release namespace from the selected context's Ranger admin credential and injects tagSync.ranger.{url,existingSecret} into the values, so the tag-projector CronJob authenticates to the context's Ranger without the operator handling any credential.

Trino reads Hive tables as its own service identity (hive.hdfs.trino.principal); the Hive metastore's Ranger plugin therefore authorises that identity, not the end user. Grant it SELECT on the context's Hive repository, the way Superset's Hive connection is granted.
